 Latest updates on 2026 midterm election results:
 President Trump announced Friday that he is replacing White House chief of staff Susie Wiles with longtime aide Stephen Miller, the most significant shakeup of his team since Republicans' losses in the midterm elections.
 The extent of those losses continues to come into focus as more races in the House are decided.  Democrats flipped more than 40 Republican districts — some of which were viewed as deep red — and staved off major losses  from redistricting . Democrats will hold at least 54 Senate seats and around 256 seats in the House in January, CBS News estimates.
 More than 20 House races and two Senate contests  remain unresolved . In Mississippi's Senate race, Democrat Scott Colom leads by about 2,500 votes as ballots continue to be counted. If he ultimately prevails, it would be one of the biggest political upsets in recent memory.
 Find updates on  key House races here , and  all election results in the CBS News Election Center . 
 New Updates
 7:08 PM
 Sen. Chris Van Hollen urges colleagues to avoid rushing to select their next Senate majority leader
 Democratic Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland urged his Democratic colleagues to show restraint in the selection process of their Senate majority leader in the wake of the party's dominant showing in the midterm elections this week.
 "There should be no coronation," Van Hollen said during an interview Saturday at the Crooked Con political conference in Washington, D.C. "I said very clearly that we need to have a discussion in the Democratic Caucus. We need to understand what the Democrats are going to do with this new responsibility and these new powers, and that nobody should get a blank check without a full understanding from the caucus as to where we're going to go."
 The Democrats will hold at least 54 seats in the upper chamber when the new session of Congress convenes in January. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer has led the Senate Democratic Caucus since 2017, but several incoming Democratic Senators-elect have signaled they want to see new leadership.
 "This is why I said it's really important that people withhold any commitments on the Senate leadership races until we have a chance to hear from our new members who just got off the campaign trail and have been directly in touch with voters," Van Hollen said.
 On Friday, a Van Hollen aide told CBS News the Maryland senator will not pursue the majority leadership post.

 6:30 PM / November 7, 2026
 Sen. Mark Kelly says he is considering 2028 presidential bid
 Democratic Sen. Mark Kelly of Arizona disclosed Saturday he is considering a 2028 presidential run.
 "I am thinking about it," Kelly said when asked in an interview at Crooked Con, a political conference held in Washington, D.C., hosted by the media group Crooked Media.
 The 62-year-old Kelly, a former NASA astronaut and Navy combat pilot, was among those being considered as the running mate of then-Vice President Kamala Harris in 2024 when she replaced former President Joe Biden as the Democratic presidential nominee.
 "We've had conversations," Kelly added. "We're going to continue to have."

 3:27 PM / November 7, 2026
 Trump claims Alaska Senate race "is over" but counting is still underway
 President Trump weighed in on the Alaska Senate race on Saturday, claiming that the incumbent, Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan, has won, even though counting is still underway.
 "Daniel Sullivan is leading substantially in the Alaska Senatorial Race. When you add Daniel (3,600, 1.68%) into Dan, and Gerald Heikes (4,846, 2.27%), Senator Dan Sullivan is up by thousands of Votes," Mr. Trump said in a Truth Social post. "I don't know what takes so long to announce his win."
 The contest that has garnered widespread attention over the two candidates named Dan Sullivan faces a lengthy ballot-counting process. Alaska has a ranked-choice voting system , which allows voters to rank as many or as few candidates as they'd like in order of preference.
 Approximately 74% of the votes have been counted as of Saturday, according to The Associated Press.
 Democrat Mary Peltola is leading Sen. Sullivan by over 600 votes, which is shy of the 50% of votes required to win.
 If nobody wins an outright majority once all the votes are counted, the count goes to a second round. The candidate with the fewest votes is eliminated, and their supporters' votes are redistributed to their second choice. That process continues until one candidate wins a majority.
 "This should be immediate! Anyone voting for Daniel J. Sullivan, Jr., a man who tried to change his middle initial, but was unable to get it done in time, and who was otherwise nonpolitical – Never even voted – is a vote for Senator Dan Sullivan," Mr. Trump said Saturday. "The Alaska Race is OVER. Dan Sullivan WON, BY A LOT!"

 2:37 PM / November 7, 2026
 Talarico visits memorial of Houston man killed by ICE in first public appearance since election night
 Texas Sen.-elect James Talarico visited the memorial of a father who was shot and killed in July by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer in Houston on Saturday.
 Talarico joined hundreds of others in placing his "I voted" sticker at the memorial of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, his campaign said in a statement. The visit is Talarico's first public appearance since election night, when he defeated Republican Ken Paxton and flipped the seat for Democrats for the first time since 1988 .
 "Lorenzo Salgado lived in this country for 35 years. As a construction worker, he sent his three boys to college. Lorenzo Salgado embodied the American dream. He was a child of God, endowed with infinite worth. Lorenzo, our fellow Texan, deserves justice — and that's exactly what I'll fight for in the U.S. Senate," Talarico said in a statement.
 The visit also marks four months since Salgado Araujo was killed in Magnolia Park, a neighborhood that has been a hub for the Mexican American community for a century.

 Updated 2:07 PM / November 7, 2026
 Trump to order DOJ to investigate impeachment threats
 President Trump said Saturday that he is ordering the Department of Justice to "look into" what he describes as threats by Democrats to impeach senior Republican figures, calling them "extortion at the highest level."
 In a Truth Social post , Mr. Trump said Democrats are "threatening a lot of people, including the Attorney General of the United States, and others" with impeachment and "many other forms of punishment, even though they admit they have no reason to do so."
 "There have been no impeachable acts committed, or even thought of, by the victims of this illegal process," he said. "This is extortion at the highest level, and they should be held accountable for this."
 Mr. Trump accused Democrats of also threatening GOP donors with imprisonment and other punishments "just because they happen to be Republicans, or Republican supporters."
 "This is Weaponization and Lawfare at another level," he wrote, adding that it was the Democrats who should be facing "imprisonment" and calling them "EXTORTIONISTS", writing in his trademark capital letters.
 The president's post comes just days after Democrats laid out plans to investigate Mr. Trump and others in the administration.
 They said the subjects they would focus on would include the Trump family's business dealings, corporate corruption, actions of the Department of Homeland Security and Immigration and Customs Enforcement, and the Jeffrey Epstein scandal. 
 Rep. Robert Garcia of California, who will chair the House Oversight Committee next Congress, singled out Stephen Miller, Corey Lewandowski, Kristi Noem and Trump family members as particular individuals they would target. Miller was named Mr. Trump's chief of staff on Friday.

 Republican Rep. Mike Kennedy wins reelection in Utah's 4th District
 Republican Rep. Mike Kennedy has won reelection in Utah's 4th Congressional District, CBS News projected.
 Kennedy, who previously served in the Utah state Senate and House, beat out challenges from Democrat Jonny Larsen, Independent Steven Burt and Libertarian Taylor Wright.
 "Thank you, Utah! I'm humbled by your trust and grateful for the opportunity to continue serving you in Congress," Kennedy wrote in an Instagram post after his win.

 Rep. Aisha Wahab wins full term in California's 14th District
 Democrat Rep. Aisha Wahab wins reelection to the U.S. House in California's 14th district, CBS News projected.
 Wahab beat fellow Democrat Melissa Hernandez in a rematch of August's special election  to fill the seat vacated by former Rep. Eric Swalwell.
 The embattled lawmaker resigned in April  amid sexual misconduct allegations, which he has denied.
 Wahab, the first Afghan American elected to Congress, previously served in the California state Senate.

 Trump told 60 Minutes he was planning some post-midterm firings. Hours later, he announced Susie Wiles' departure.
 President Trump announced that Stephen Miller would replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff just hours after he told 60 Minutes that he'd be shaking up his team.
 When 60 Minutes Correspondent Ross Douthat asked Mr. Trump whether he expected to fire anyone after Republicans lost both chambers of Congress, the president said: "I do, yeah. Little bit."
 "I love my Cabinet. I think they're good," he said. "But I'll … be doing maybe a few changes."

 11:26 PM / November 6, 2026
 Trump says "the Senate has to act" before new Congress takes office
 Asked about his priorities for the lame-duck session before Democrats take control of the House and Senate, President Trump told reporters : "The Senate has to act."
 "The Senate is getting nothing passed, and it's just killing our country," he said, calling the upper chamber a "roadblock" and "one of the problems we had" in the midterms. He later pointed to the SAVE America Act, a package of voting restrictions that Mr. Trump pressed Senate Republicans to take up for months, though Senate Majority Leader John Thune said it couldn't pass.
 "We had a bad election because of a few things. One thing was not getting things approved in the Senate," he later said.
 Mr. Trump called Thune a "good man," but said he's "got to get things done." Asked if Thune is the right person to serve as Senate GOP leader, he said: "It's going to be up to the Republicans. They choose, I don't choose."

 Democrats flip outgoing GOP Rep. Nancy Mace's South Carolina district
 Democrat Nancy Lacore beat Republican Jenny Costa Honeycutt in South Carolina's 1st District, CBS News projected. 
 The seat is currently held by GOP Rep. Nancy Mace, who lost her primary earlier this year for South Carolina governor. 
 Lacore, a former Navy admiral, was fired during Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's tenure.

 6:04 PM / November 6, 2026
 GOP Sen. Ron Johnson seeks to delay leadership elections
 Republican Sen. Ron Johnson of Wisconsin wants to delay next week's Senate GOP leadership elections after Tuesday's electoral bloodbath. 
 "There's no reason to rush into the elections, particularly after stunning defeat," Johnson said in an interview Friday on "The Takeout with Major Garrett." 
 Johnson said he's writing a letter to leadership to request the postponement and that at least five of his Republican colleagues have signed on to it. He said the letter is not "hostile" to Senate Majority Leader John Thune or other leaders. 
 "All I'm asking is, we have the very robust discussion that we should have after stunning defeat, before we move into leadership elections," Johnson said. "We don't even know how many people are in our conference yet. We may not know for a couple weeks. Again, there's no reason to rush into these leadership elections now. There's a lot of reason for robust discussion and reflection about what went wrong." 
 The results of two Senate races in Mississippi and Alaska — where GOP incumbents are facing possible defeat — have yet to be determined.

 Stephen Miller after midterm losses: We must "fight with all of our soul" to support Trump
 In his first statement on his new role as White House chief of staff, Stephen Miller said, "The mission now is more clear than ever: Fight with all of our soul to support our President and defend this magnificent Republic." 
 Miller is set to take over the role Monday, replacing Susie Wiles, who is leaving after Republicans suffered major losses in the midterm elections. 
 Miller also praised Wiles, calling her "incomparable."

 Top Democrat on House Oversight Committee: "Stephen Miller should lawyer up"
 In a sign of how Stephen Miller's promotion is being received among Democrats, Rep. Robert Garcia of California vowed to launch investigations into Miller's actions in the White House. Garcia is the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee and is poised to become its chairman in the next Congress.
 "Just days after the American people rejected his corrupt and lawless presidency, Donald Trump is doubling down. Stephen Miller is the architect of the unconstitutional ICE raids that have terrorized our communities and kidnapped and killed American citizens and immigrant families," Garcia said. "Oversight Democrats will continue to investigate Miller for his misconduct, and we will fight against his hateful policies in Congress and the courts."
 He added: "Stephen Miller should lawyer up."

 Trump names Stephen Miller chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles
 President Trump announced Stephen Miller will replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff, the most significant shakeup yet since Republicans' losses in the midterm elections.
 "I am pleased to announce that Mr. Stephen Miller, the current Deputy Chief of Staff of the Trump Administration, and one of my most trusted advisors, will become the Chief of Staff starting Monday, November 9, 2026," the president wrote on Truth Social . "Susie Wiles, who has done an outstanding job, will be moving over to the Trump Political Operation. I want to thank her for her service as Chief of Staff — She has done a great job!"

 Sunday: Trump talks to 60 Minutes' Ross Douthat in first sit-down interview since midterms
 Sunday on 60 Minutes, hear from President Trump in his first sit-down interview since Democrats' sweeping midterm victories.
 60 Minutes Correspondent Ross Douthat interviewed Mr. Trump at the White House on Friday about Republican losses, congressional investigations, the wars in Iran and Ukraine, and the economy.

 1:22 PM / November 6, 2026
 DOJ exodus continues with resignations of 2 more senior officials
 Two more senior officials at the Department of Justice have resigned, following the departure of Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon on Thursday.
 Jon Eisenberg, the assistant attorney general in charge of the National Security Division, resigned on Friday, Attorney General Todd Blanche said on X . Blanche did not give a reason for his departure but thanked him for "strengthening our nation's ability to address threats, both foreign and domestic."
 Jason Reding Quiñones also submitted his resignation as the top federal prosecutor in South Florida. Quiñones was overseeing the so-called "grand conspiracy" investigation into Obama- and Biden-era intelligence officials. Blanche praised him for his work tackling violent crime, trafficking and transnational criminal organizations.
 Read more about Eisenberg's resignation here , and Quiñones' departure here .

 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/midterm-election-results-2026-democrats-house-senate-trump/#post-update-0b145335

 11:58 AM / November 6, 2026
 Scott Wiener wins California seat to replace Nancy Pelosi
 California state Sen. Scott Wiener has won the race to succeed former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi in Congress, CBS News projected.
 Wiener claimed victory earlier in the week after his opponent, San Francisco Supervisor Connie Chan, conceded the race.
 Wiener will represent California's 11th Congressional District, which covers most of San Francisco. Pelosi is retiring after nearly 40 years of serving in the House of Representatives. 
 "I'm humbled to carry forward the powerful legacy of this seat — Phil Burton, Sala Burton, and the greatest Speaker in modern American history, Nancy Pelosi," Wiener said in a statement on Wednesday. "Speaker Pelosi came to Congress to fight AIDS when too many wanted to look away, and she never stopped fighting for our city and our country. Madame Speaker, thank you."

 11:38 AM / November 6, 2026
 Mississippi continuing to process absentee mail-in ballots and affidavit ballots
 Mississippi is continuing to process absentee mail-in ballots and to verify affidavit ballots. 
 Mississippi Secretary of State Michael Watson said 6,936 affidavit ballots have now been processed, with roughly 80% of them accepted. And about 3,300 absentee mail-in ballots are still out. 
 The Senate race between incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith and Democrat Scott Colom is still a toss-up, according to CBS News' rating.

 11:20 AM / November 6, 2026
 Van Hollen won't challenge Schumer for majority leader
 Democratic Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland will not pursue a role in Senate Democratic leadership, an aide said, although he "believes the caucus needs to have an honest and open conversation about how we move an agenda forward that reflects the will of the American people."
 "[Van Hollen has] made it clear that the new Democratic majorities need to use their power to push a proactive, economic agenda," the aide said. "As the Senator has said publicly, he is not looking at the majority leader role and is actively 'kicking the tires' on the 2028 presidential election to shape the direction of the party and the country as we fight to end a rigged economy and overhaul a corrupt political system."
 Several incoming senators have said they will not support current Democratic leader Sen. Chuck Schumer as majority leader, but a viable challenger has yet to emerge.
 By
 Ibrahim Aksoy 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/midterm-election-results-2026-democrats-house-senate-trump/#post-update-b8659a09

 9:58 AM / November 6, 2026
 Acton says she has "no intention" of speaking to Ramaswamy after "terrible and despicable" ad featuring her mother
 Ohio's Democratic Gov.-elect Amy Acton said Friday that she has "no intention" of speaking to Vivek Ramaswamy, her Republican opponent in the governor's race, after he ran what she called a "terrible and despicable" ad featuring her estranged mother.
 In her first TV interview on "CBS Mornings," Acton was asked whether she had spoken to Ramaswamy since she defeated him in Tuesday's election . Ramaswamy said during his concession speech that he called Acton and left her a message to congratulate her on her win.
 "I have no intention of speaking to him," Acton said. "I do believe that leaders' words matter, and we need to hold folks accountable."
 The Ohio governor's race garnered heightened national attention in the final days of the campaign when Ramaswamy ran an attack ad featuring Acton's estranged mother, Donna Arthur, who called her daughter a "liar." 
 But Acton had not seen Arthur since she was 12 years old. Acton and her brother had been removed from their mother's care after their stepfather, Cledith Arthur, was arrested and charged with raping Acton when she was between 10 and 12 years old. Acton's brother said that their birth mother remained married to him until his death in 2004.
 Watch the interview here. 
 By

 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/midterm-election-results-2026-democrats-house-senate-trump/#post-update-055955ae

 9:52 AM / November 6, 2026
 The House and Senate races that don't have winners yet
 The exact margins of the Democratic majorities in Congress aren't yet settled, since winners have not yet been projected in two Senate races and more than two dozen House races. They include GOP-held districts with razor-thin margins, a few Democratic seats that could flip to Republicans and several races in California and other Western states that still need to count ballots. 
 Here are the congressional races that CBS News has not yet projected, including where the results stand.

 12:39 AM / November 6, 2026
 Judge blocks DOJ from demanding election workers in Washington reject certain ballots
 U.S. District Judge Jamal Whitehead granted a temporary restraining order blocking the Justice Department from demanding that election workers in Washington state reject ballots of voters suspected of being noncitizens. The department was also barred from threatening workers with prosecution if they don't comply.
 "Plaintiffs are likely to succeed on their claim that Defendants have exceeded their authority, and the harm to Washington voters whose ballots are set aside on the strength of an unreliable federal list cannot be undone after the fact," Whitehead wrote in the ruling , which came in a lawsuit filed by several groups.
 Prior to Election Day, the Justice Department pushed officials in multiple states to crack down on alleged voting by non-citizens. Federal prosecutors in Washington asked the state's top election official last week to set aside ballots from more than 400 people who they believe aren't citizens . State officials responded that "many of the persons on your list are United States citizens" and a "significant number" aren't registered to vote in the state.
 By
 Jacob Rosen , Joe Walsh 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/midterm-election-results-2026-democrats-house-senate-trump/#post-update-68c86758

 8:34 PM / November 5, 2026
 What Trump's final 2 years in office will look like with Democrats in charge
 President Trump seems to be reconsidering his approach to Democrats after Tuesday's massive Republican election losses and has so far made contradictory comments about how he plans to deal with them as they take control of the Senate and the House in January. 
 "We're going to work with the Democrats," the president told Politico as GOP defeats were beginning to stack up Tuesday night, though in a phone call with CBS News' Robert Costa before polls closed, he had said, "I have the ultimate power — it's called 'veto.'" 
 By Wednesday afternoon, he had merged the two approaches.
 "I'll get along, probably, with the Democrats, unless they want to be destructive, but I have the power of the veto," the president told reporters at the White House ballroom construction site Wednesday. On Thursday, a red hat that said "VETO" sat on the Resolute Desk in the Oval Office.
 But Democrats may not be the only source of friction ahead. After two years of working in lockstep with Mr. Trump, some Republicans may prove more willing to defy the term-limited president to try to salvage their political careers. 
 Read more here .
 By
 Caitlin Yilek , Kathryn Watson 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/midterm-election-results-2026-democrats-house-senate-trump/#post-update-08b628d4 
 link copied 
 7:42 PM / November 5, 2026
 Where the razor-thin Mississippi Senate race stands
 The U.S. Senate race in Mississippi remains a toss-up between incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith and Democrat Scott Colom , with Colom leading by fewer than 2,000 votes.
 According to Mississippi Secretary of State Michael Watson , there are approximately 3,600 outstanding mail ballots and an unknown number of affidavit ballots, or provisional ballots, from voters whose eligibility needs to be confirmed. Absentee ballots must be received within five business days, while affidavit ballots must be processed within the 10-day window that counties have to certify results, which ends Nov. 13. 
 Both parties are keeping a close eye on the process. CBS News has confirmed the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee has deployed lawyers and resources to the state to monitor the count.
 "I'm confident that ultimately Mississippi has decided to go in a new direction," Colom told reporters after greeting campaign volunteers Thursday morning in Jackson. 
 The National Republican Senatorial Committee and Hyde-Smith campaign filed a request for all counties to separate and preserve all affidavit ballots. The Colom campaign called the move a "desperate stunt."  His counsel also sent a new letter to Mississippi's 82 counties asking them to respect election procedures. 
 Hyde-Smith predicted that she will represent Mississippi for another six-year term, posting on X : "We believe thousands of votes remain to be counted from dozens of Republican counties, and we are confident those votes will reinforce her path to victory."
 At a news conference Thursday, Mississippi Republican Party Chair Mike Hurst insisted the election "is far from being over" and noted the state party has attorneys and observers throughout the state to ensure all legally cast ballots are counted.
 Mississippi does not allow recounts, so a winner will be decided based on a plurality of votes.
 By
 Nikole Killion 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/midterm-election-results-2026-democrats-house-senate-trump/#post-update-0a37292e

 7:11 PM / November 5, 2026
 Democrats have now flipped over 40 House seats
 Democrats won control of the House of Representatives by picking up perennial swing districts and seats that were once considered deep red. The party's wins ranged from suburban areas in the northeastern United States to areas of South Texas that were once viewed as increasingly GOP-friendly.
 So far, 43 districts have shifted to Democrats and two have shifted to Republicans. Winners in dozens of races have yet to be projected.

 6:23 PM / November 5, 2026
 Rep. Anna Paulina Luna narrowly wins reelection
 GOP Rep. Anna Paulina Luna narrowly won her race in Florida's 13th District, CBS News projected. With 99% of the votes counted, Luna was leading by less than one point. 
 She faced Democrat Leela Gray.
 By
 Caitlin Yilek 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/midterm-election-results-2026-democrats-house-senate-trump/#post-update-8b972fe5 
 link copied 
 6:22 PM / November 5, 2026
 GOP Rep. Mike Lawler defeated in New York battleground district
